sections.label: Corporate Income Tax rebate changes
sections.summary: The CIT rebate cap rises from $20,000 to $25,000 at 50% for YA2017, and is extended to YA2018 at 20% capped at $10,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: First, the existing Corporate Income Tax (CIT) rebate for Year of Assessment (YA) 2017 is enhanced by raising the cap from $20,000 to $25,000, while keeping the rebate percentage unchanged at 50%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The CIT rebate will also be extended to YA2018, at 20% of tax payable, capped at $10,000.

sections.label: Personal Income Tax rebate
sections.summary: A 20% Personal Income Tax rebate capped at $500 per taxpayer is granted to all individual tax residents for YA2017.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Third, to provide relief to individuals who pay income tax, a Personal Income Tax rebate of 20% of tax payable will be granted to all individual tax residents for YA2017, capped at $500 per taxpayer.

sections.label: Additional MediSave Contribution Scheme cap
sections.summary: From 1 January 2018, the maximum voluntary employer contribution to an employee's MediSave account under the scheme rises from $1,500 to $2,730 per year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Second, with effect from 1 January 2018, the Government will raise the maximum amount that an employer can voluntarily contribute to his employee’s MediSave account under the Additional MediSave Contribution Scheme from $1,500 to $2,730 per year.

sections.label: MediSave scheme contribution and deduction raised
sections.summary: From 1 January 2018, the maximum employer MediSave contribution not treated as employee income rises from $1,500 to $2,730 yearly, with tax deduction raised accordingly.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This national medical savings scheme has helped to address the basic medical expenses for hospitalisation, surgeries and outpatient expenses for many Singaporeans and their loved ones.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am, therefore, pleased to note that with effect from 1 January 2018, the maximum amount that an employer can contribute to his employee’s MediSave account that is not treated as income of the employee under the Additional MediSave Contribution Scheme will be raised from $1,500 to $2,730 per year, and the tax deduction allowable will also be raised accordingly.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Hopefully, this will encourage more employers to increase contributions to their employees’ MediSave accounts.

sections.label: Other ways to encourage employers
sections.summary: The passage asks whether other ways besides tax deductions can be explored to encourage employers to contribute.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Aside from tax deductions, can we explore other ways to encourage employers to do so?

sections.label: Stepping up publicity
sections.summary: The passage asks how the authorities can step up the publicity.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: How can the authorities step up the publicity?

sections.label: Corporate income tax rebate changes
sections.summary: The corporate income tax rebate cap rises from $20,000 to $25,000, the 50% rate stays, and the rebate is extended to YA2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government has raised the corporate income tax rebate cap from $20,000 to $25,000, with the rebate rate unchanged at 50%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The rebate will also be extended by another year till YA2018.

sections.label: Safe harbour rule for cost sharing
sections.summary: After amendment, the Government will adopt the safe harbour rule for expenditure covered by cost sharing agreements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: After amendment, the Government will adopt the “safe harbour rule for expenditure covered by cost sharing agreements”.

sections.label: Refinements to business hub tax incentives
sections.summary: Among 25 changed tax measures, several refine existing tax incentives for specific business hub activities such as infrastructure financing, project financing, commodity trading, maritime, finance, insurance and aircraft leasing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Amongst the 25 tax measures that have undergone changes in this Bill, quite a number are refinements to the existing tax incentives for specific business hub activities, including infrastructure financing, project financing, commodity trading, maritime, finance, insurance and aircraft leasing.

sections.label: MediSave tax deduction increase
sections.summary: The increase in the maximum tax deductible amount for employers and self-employed persons would encourage voluntary contribution towards MediSave.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The increase in the maximum tax deductible amount for both employers and self-employed persons would encourage voluntary contribution towards MediSave.

sections.label: R&D tax exemption importance
sections.summary: Clause 12 amends section 14DA, and tax exemption for R&D is important in encouraging innovation even in a slowing economy.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As for clause 12 in the Income Tax (Amendment) Bill to amend section 14DA, tax-exemption for R&D is important in encouraging innovation even in a slowing economy to empower the continual transformation of our industries and economy.

sections.label: Dependant income criterion increase suggestion
sections.summary: A speaker suggests raising the $4,000 annual income criterion for individuals with dependants to reflect cost of living and rising healthcare costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Though our median wage has risen beyond $3,000, it is imperative to note that as the population continues to age, the burden on children in smaller families grows exponentially, even more so, as our average lifespan increases beyond 80.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I suggest we consider increasing the annual income criterion set at $4,000 for individuals with dependants to be reflective of cost of living and rising healthcare cost.

sections.label: Related party transaction provision
sections.summary: The new related party transaction provision shows IRAS is ahead of the curve and strengthens Singapore's reputation as a responsible tax jurisdiction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new provision to strengthen related party transaction shows that IRAS is ahead of the curve, and it strengthens Singapore's reputation as a responsible tax jurisdiction.

sections.label: Amendment Bill and BEPS
sections.summary: The amendment Bill is worthy of support as a step in deterring profit-shifting and aligning practices with OECD BEPS developments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As such, this amendment Bill is worthy of support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This is a significant step in deterring and addressing profit-shifting behaviour, and would align our practices more closely with international tax developments under the OECD's Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) initiative.

sections.label: Section 34F(8) TPD offences
sections.summary: New section 34F(8) deems failure to meet certain TPD requirements as offences with a fine of up to $10,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Next, the new section 34F(8) deems the failure to meet certain TPD requirements as offences and provides for a fine of up to $10,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As the TPD requirement only applies to businesses with gross revenue exceeding $10 million, a fine of up to $10,000 may not represent a significant cost.

sections.label: Penal Code falsification offence
sections.summary: Falsification of accounts under section 477A of the Penal Code may attract up to 10 years' imprisonment, or a fine, or both.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For comparison, the offence of falsification of accounts under section 477A of the Penal Code may attract imprisonment for a term of up to 10 years, or a fine, or both.

sections.label: TPD penalties and arm's length principle
sections.summary: The TPD penalties are in line with support of the arm's length principle, higher than record keeping penalties and comparable with similar jurisdictions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Therefore, in introducing this new requirement for TPD, the penalties for failure to comply with such requirements are in line with our clear and strong support of the arm's length principle.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: These penalties are higher than the existing penalties under the record keeping requirement and also comparable with the range of penalties imposed by jurisdictions with similar requirements.

sections.label: MediSave voluntary contributions 2016
sections.summary: In 2016, over 640 companies made voluntary MediSave contributions, up 11% from 580 in 2015, benefiting 28,000 employees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In 2016, more than 640 companies made voluntary MediSave contributions, an 11% increase from the 580 companies that did so in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In addition, 28,000 employees benefited from those contributions in 2016, a 6% increase from the 26,500 employees who did so in 2015.

sections.label: Additional MediSave Contribution scheme outreach
sections.summary: From 1 January 2018, higher voluntary MediSave contributions and tax deductions apply, and MOM, CPF Board and tripartite partners will reach out to employers to raise awareness.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: With the increase in the maximum amount of voluntary MediSave contributions that a company can make under the Additional MediSave Contribution scheme and a corresponding increase in tax deduction allowable with effect from 1 January 2018, the Ministry of Manpower and Central Provident Fund Board, together with the tripartite partners, will further reach out to all employers through website, emails, letters, seminars and talks to both raise awareness of the scheme and communicate the change and limits.
